Hi Alex / Sophie,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really appreciate the deep dive on your customer UX requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on a short PoC: 

Recap (what I heard)
- Primary goal: streaming responses with a perceptually instant first token (TTFT) for chat-like UX.
- Target TTFT: ~< 150ms for interactive sessions on average; 99th percentile target TBD but aiming for <300ms in your primary region.
- Concurrency/throughput: typical concurrency ~50 active user streams in peak, but burst to 100; peak request QPS ~200.
- Response size: median response ~150 tokens; some long responses up to ~8k tokens for summaries.
- Streaming requirements: browser clients prefer WebSocket for persistent streams, but SSE acceptable for simple flows. Chunk cadence should feel smooth (rough target: 150–300ms between chunks for long responses).
- Non-functional: SOC 2 + encryption at rest/in transit required.

Questions / clarifications for you
1) Can you confirm that WebSocket is acceptable in your webapp, or do you need SSE-only?
2) For the 99th percentile TTFT target: is <300ms acceptable as a starting SLO while we tune?
3) Any strict per-request token limits we should be aware of (e.g., maximum 8k tokens vs 16k)?

Proposed next steps (short PoC plan)
- Redwood to run a short synthetic perf run using your sample payloads and our recommended model/instance profile. Deliverables: perf run report (TTFT distribution, p50/p90/p99 latencies, throughput numbers), suggested config for streaming chunk cadence, and recommended instance sizing.
- We’ll provide a test harness (scripts + sample payloads) and a shared Drive link. 
- Schedule a follow-up to review results and agree on any infra changes (target: 1 week).

Attachments: redwood-perf-proposal.xlsx (test plan & instance sizing), sample-payloads.json (examples to run).

If that plan looks good I’ll coordinate with Rishi to schedule the perf run — ideally we’ll run from a US region to match your users.

Thanks,

Hi Alex — looping in a short technical note and the perf plan. Forwarding Marissa’s summary below.

Technical notes / recommendations
- WebSocket vs SSE: WebSockets give lower reconnection overhead and better control frames (recommended for analytics). SSE has slightly simpler deployment for static sites but can exhibit larger head-of-line delays in some proxies. For the PoC we’ll run WebSocket tests first.
- TTFT levers: small things that often move TTFT substantially: model compilation (pre-warmed kernels), KV/prefix caching for repeated prompts, and bumping CPU threads for network handling on the worker. We’ll test with/without prefix caching to benchmark delta.
- Chunk cadence: chunk size vs cadence tradeoff — sending smaller chunks (~150–300ms cadence) feels smoother but increases per-token overhead. We’ll measure bytes-per-chunk and cadence; our suggested default cadence for chat is 200ms.
- Measurement: we’ll report client-observed TTFT (time from request to first byte in client) and server-side generation first-token time. Both matter — network can add ~10–40ms depending on region.

Perf run proposal (attached):
- Synthetic test: 10k requests at concurrency 50, sustained for 10 minutes, with a spike test to 120 concurrent sessions for 2 minutes.
- Model/profile: redwood-faststream-v1, quantized low-latency profile.
- Metrics: TTFT distribution (client/server), chunk cadence histogram, throughput, p50/p90/p99 tail latencies, memory/CPU/GPU utilization.

Please confirm the preferred run time (July 14 or 15) and send staging IPs for allowlist. Once we have that we’ll share the perf scripts and kick off the run.

Thanks — rishi
